comment: Hand-kept statuses for packages/ghostty_dart_xterm/COMPATIBILITY.md (tool/xterm_compat/compat.dart, rules in src/compare.dart). Keys: a library (zmodem.dart), a symbol (Terminal) or a member (Terminal.write; Terminal.new is the unnamed constructor). status: differs (present, behaves differently), missing (planned), wont (not provided, on purpose). A missing member without an entry is missing/planned. Signature differences are found automatically and need no entry. Regenerate with `mise run compat`.

zmodem.dart.reason: needs package:zmodem as a new dependency, a separate decision (ADR 0013)

utils.dart.reason: the debugger is built on xterm's Dart escape parser; parsing lives in libghostty-vt (ADR 0004, ADR 0013)

EscapeHandler.reason: parsing lives in libghostty-vt, so there is no handler to implement or subclass (ADR 0004, ADR 0013)

Buffer.charset.reason: charset state lives in libghostty-vt; xterm's Charset type is not exported either

TerminalViewState.renderTerminal.reason: xterm's render object (RenderTerminal, not exported); the view renders through ghostty_dart_flutter (ADR 0011)

Terminal.reason: not an EscapeHandler: its handler methods write the equivalent sequence while the parser is in its ground state and throw StateError otherwise (ADR 0013)

Terminal.onIconChange.reason: only setIconName calls it: libghostty-vt 1.0.0 does not report the icon name of OSC 0 and OSC 1 (ADR 0013 known limits)

Terminal.mainBuffer.reason: while the alternate screen is active it reads as blank lines (cursor at 0, 0) and its mutators throw StateError: libghostty-vt 1.0.0 exposes only the active screen (ADR 0013 known limits)

Terminal.reflowEnabled.reason: applies to Terminal.resize only (a TerminalView's resizes always reflow), and without reflow libghostty-vt drops the cells beyond a narrower width instead of keeping them for a later, wider resize (ADR 0013 known limits)

Terminal.onPrivateOSC.reason: only sees OSC sequences that libghostty-vt does not implement itself (ADR 0013 known limits)

Terminal.onResize.reason: Terminal.resize passes its own arguments, as in xterm; when a TerminalView resizes the terminal, the pixel arguments are the cell size in logical pixels from the view's device pixel ratio, and it is called only when the size changed (ADR 0013)

Terminal.unknownCSI.reason: no-op, as in xterm, and never called by parsing: libghostty-vt parses (ADR 0013)

Terminal.unsupportedStyle.reason: no-op, as in xterm, and never called by parsing: libghostty-vt parses (ADR 0013)

Buffer.marginTop.reason: libghostty-vt 1.0.0 does not expose the DECSTBM scroll margins (ADR 0013 known limits)

Buffer.marginBottom.reason: libghostty-vt 1.0.0 does not expose the DECSTBM scroll margins (ADR 0013 known limits)

Buffer.absoluteMarginTop.reason: libghostty-vt 1.0.0 does not expose the DECSTBM scroll margins (ADR 0013 known limits)

Buffer.absoluteMarginBottom.reason: libghostty-vt 1.0.0 does not expose the DECSTBM scroll margins (ADR 0013 known limits)

KeytabInputHandler.call.reason: application cursor keys follow cursorKeysMode (DECCKM); xterm reads appKeypadMode there, a bug (ADR 0013)

ClickMouseHandler.call.reason: normal and UTF-8 mouse reports encode the row as 32 + y; xterm sends 32 + y + 1, an off-by-one (ADR 0013)

UpDownMouseHandler.call.reason: normal and UTF-8 mouse reports encode the row as 32 + y; xterm sends 32 + y + 1, an off-by-one (ADR 0013)

TerminalView.reason: keys typed into the view are encoded by libghostty-vt (Kitty protocol, key releases) while terminal.inputHandler is defaultInputHandler; mouse reports come from libghostty-vt's encoder; one TerminalView per Terminal (ADR 0013)

TerminalView.scrollController.reason: accepted and ignored: libghostty-vt owns scrolling (ADR 0011, ADR 0013)

Terminal.altBuffer.reason: while the main screen is active it reads as blank lines (cursor at 0, 0) and its mutators throw StateError: libghostty-vt 1.0.0 exposes only the active screen (ADR 0013 known limits)

Terminal.unknownSBC.reason: no-op, as in xterm, and never called by parsing: libghostty-vt parses (ADR 0013)

Terminal.unkownEscape.reason: no-op, as in xterm, and never called by parsing: libghostty-vt parses (ADR 0013)

Terminal.setUnknownMode.reason: no-op, as in xterm, and never called by parsing: libghostty-vt parses (ADR 0013)

Terminal.setUnknownDecMode.reason: no-op, as in xterm, and never called by parsing: libghostty-vt parses (ADR 0013)

Terminal.setColumnMode.reason: no-op, as in xterm, and never called by parsing: libghostty-vt parses (ADR 0013)

Terminal.maxLines.reason: approximate: libghostty-vt drops scrollback in whole pages, so more lines are kept (about 300 at 80 columns with maxLines: 30); there is no byte limit

Terminal.cursor.reason: a new copy of the SGR pen on every read: changing it does not change the terminal; palette colours 0-15 read as named colours (libghostty-vt does not tell SGR 31 from SGR 38;5;1)

Terminal.write.reason: events the output raises (onBell, onTitleChange, onOutput replies, onPrivateOSC, onResize) are delivered in order after the chunk is parsed, not during parsing; replies to queries are libghostty-vt's (ADR 0013)

Terminal.onOutput.reason: bytes from libghostty-vt (keys and mouse reports typed into a TerminalView, replies to queries) are decoded as UTF-8, or Latin-1 for a chunk that is not valid UTF-8; onOutputBytes (an addition) has the exact bytes (ADR 0013)

Terminal.lines.reason: a read-only view: lines are snapshots made on first access (one native read per cell, about 50 us per 80-column line in a debug build) and are no longer attached once the terminal changes (ADR 0013)

Terminal.writeChar.reason: writes the character through libghostty-vt's parser; a control character is dropped (xterm stores it as a glyph)

Terminal.setTitle.reason: writes OSC 2, which calls onTitleChange; control characters in the title are dropped

Terminal.moveCursorY.reason: CUU/CUD stop at the scroll region's margins (xterm clamps to the screen only)

Terminal.cursorNextLine.reason: CUU/CUD stop at the scroll region's margins (xterm clamps to the screen only)

Terminal.cursorPrecedingLine.reason: CUU/CUD stop at the scroll region's margins (xterm clamps to the screen only)

Terminal.setMargins.reason: writes DECSTBM and moves the cursor back; libghostty-vt ignores a one-line region (top == bottom)

Buffer.reason: a view of a libghostty-vt screen: lines are read on demand; the mutators write the equivalent escape sequence (active buffer only, StateError otherwise or while the output stopped inside a sequence); a Buffer created for another TerminalState holds blank lines (ADR 0013)

Buffer.lines.reason: a read-only view: lines are snapshots made on first access (one native read per cell, about 50 us per 80-column line in a debug build) and are no longer attached once the terminal changes (ADR 0013)

Buffer.write.reason: writes through libghostty-vt's parser; control characters are dropped (xterm stores them as glyphs)

Buffer.writeChar.reason: writes through libghostty-vt's parser; control characters are dropped (xterm stores them as glyphs)

Buffer.backspace.reason: BS: does not move back onto a soft-wrapped previous line (xterm does)

Buffer.cursorGoForward.reason: CUF 1: stops at the last column (xterm can enter the pending-wrap state)

Buffer.moveCursorY.reason: CUU/CUD stop at the scroll region's margins (xterm clamps to the screen only)

Buffer.moveCursor.reason: CUU/CUD stop at the scroll region's margins (xterm clamps to the screen only)

Buffer.setVerticalMargins.reason: writes DECSTBM and moves the cursor back; libghostty-vt ignores a one-line region (top == bottom)

Buffer.isInVerticalMargin.reason: always true: libghostty-vt 1.0.0 does not expose the DECSTBM scroll margins (ADR 0013 known limits)

Buffer.clear.reason: writes ED 2 and ED 3: the erased cells keep the current background colour; the cursor stays and anchors are detached, as in xterm

Buffer.resize.reason: one screen cannot be resized alone in libghostty-vt; Terminal.resize resizes both

Buffer.createAnchor.reason: returns an anchor tracked by libghostty-vt (see CellAnchor); it holds native memory until disposed

Buffer.createAnchorFromOffset.reason: returns an anchor tracked by libghostty-vt (see CellAnchor); it holds native memory until disposed

Buffer.createAnchorFromCursor.reason: returns an anchor tracked by libghostty-vt (see CellAnchor); it holds native memory until disposed

BufferLine.createAnchor.reason: returns an anchor tracked by libghostty-vt (see CellAnchor); it holds native memory until disposed

CellAnchor.reason: an anchor made on a terminal's line is tracked by libghostty-vt: it follows scrolling and reflow, but not lines moved by IL, DL or scroll-region scrolling, and line returns a fresh snapshot; it holds native memory until disposed (ADR 0013)

BufferLine.reason: a line read from a terminal is a snapshot: its setters change the snapshot only; a grapheme cluster keeps its first code point; every underline style reads as underline and overline is dropped (ADR 0013)

Terminal.scrollUp.reason: SU: on the main screen with a full-screen scroll region the lines scrolled off go to the scrollback (libghostty-vt); xterm drops them

Buffer.scrollUp.reason: SU: on the main screen with a full-screen scroll region the lines scrolled off go to the scrollback (libghostty-vt); xterm drops them

TerminalController.selection.reason: while a TerminalView shows the controller it is the selection on the screen (mouse selections included), read from libghostty-vt; a selection set with setSelection keeps xterm's anchors until the user changes it

TerminalController.setSelection.reason: also selects the range on the screen of the view that shows the controller; an empty range shows nothing there

TerminalController.highlight.reason: painted by ghostty_dart_flutter over the text and over the selection (xterm paints the selection last; only the blend order of translucent colours differs), and only while the screen (primary or alternate) it was made on is active

TerminalController.setSuspendPointerInpu.reason: suspending also stops wheel reports (xterm 4.0.0 still reports the wheel)

TerminalController.setPointerInputs.reason: drag and move, when enabled, are reported as motion (xterm 4.0.0 never reports them); the wheel is reported whatever the set says, as in xterm

TerminalView.onTapUp.reason: called for a click that selected nothing and was not reported to the program (xterm calls it for every tap)

TerminalView.textStyle.reason: cells are measured from the font and snapped to device pixels, so a cell can be slightly larger or smaller than xterm's for the same font

TerminalView.simulateScroll.reason: sets the default of DEC mode 1007 (alternate scroll): a program that turns 1007 on still gets arrow keys when it is false

TerminalView.shortcuts.reason: the select-all action (Ctrl+A, Cmd+A) selects the whole buffer, scrollback included (xterm: the screen); paste never asks before pasting, as in xterm

TerminalViewState.cursorRect.reason: relative to the view's top-left corner, padding included (xterm: inside TerminalView.padding); Rect.zero before the first layout (xterm throws)

TerminalViewState.globalCursorRect.reason: Rect.zero before the first layout or while the cursor is scrolled out of view (xterm throws or returns an off-screen rectangle)
